rules.when: Task needs live web facts: breaking news, current events, today's market/product state.
rules.why: Only the Grok TUI has live web access.

rules.when: Task needs generated images or visual assets: icons, illustrations, logos, mockup art, placeholder imagery.
rules.why: Only Pi with the pi-antigravity extension has a generate_image tool (saves under .pi/generated-images/). Spends the agy quota.

rules.when: Review, audit, or second opinion on a diff/PR/design another crewmate produced. Not for writing the fix.
rules.why: Review with a different model family than the author. Codex-authored work goes to Opus, Claude-authored work goes to Sol.

rules.when: Recon-only, file gathering, narrow lookup, or a trivial mechanical edit (rename, format sweep, typo fix).
rules.why: Cheapest tier. Gemini 3.8 Flash spends the separate agy quota here, where its lower coding score does not matter. Grok 4.7 here is a quota fallback, not a first pick.

rules.when: Ordinary implementation, bounded bug fix, tests, everyday coding with a clear path.
rules.why: Workhorse tier. Gemini 3.8 Flash stays out: it scores about 20 points under Sol on the Coding Agent Index. Grok 4.7 here is a quota fallback, not a first pick.

rules.when: Large/ambiguous multi-file change, risky refactor, work holding many moving parts at once.
rules.why: Same Sol model as workhorse tier, more thinking budget. Opus 5.5 via the agy harness is the same model as claude:opus but bills Antigravity's separate claude_gpt quota, so it wins while that quota lasts. Grok 4.7 here is a quota fallback, not a first pick.

rules.when: Hardest available work: root-cause investigation, architecture, ambiguous design, or already failed on the workhorse tier.
rules.why: Frontier tier, reserve for this only. GPT-6.1 Sol replaces GPT-6 Astra: it matches or beats Astra on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at a fraction of the cost per task. Never Claude fable: it stalls unattended on a usage-credit prompt.
